raw_response:
I would begin with Qwen3.5-4B in Q6_K, then compare Qwen3.5-9B in Q4_K_M if the larger model fits your actual retain workload. These are research leads, not a verified claim that either matches gpt-oss-20b in Hindsight. I found no matched retain evaluation or measured RTX 5060 8 GB configuration in the sources examined.

Ranked candidates

1. Qwen3.5-4B, Q6_K GGUF
Official model: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B
Quantization files: https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF/tree/main

This is my first trial because its Q6_K file is 3.53 GB, leaving appreciably more room for context and runtime allocations than the larger candidates. The official comparison reports IFEval of 89.8 for the 4B model against 88.2 for gpt-oss-20b. That gives a reason to investigate instruction adherence, but it is not evidence of equivalent extraction quality after quantization. Qwen3.5 thinks by default; test its supported non-thinking setting for the retain workload and check what quality changes. Its hybrid attention architecture also makes using a compatible llama.cpp build essential.

2. Qwen3.5-9B, Q4_K_M GGUF
Official model: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B
Quantization files: https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF/tree/main

This is the quality-oriented second trial. The same official comparison gives the 9B model IFEval of 91.5, and its Q4_K_M file is 5.68 GB. A fit is plausible with bounded context, but the file size is not a VRAM measurement. Treat the 9B configuration as conditional until the maximum retain input and output complete without weight, cache, or tensor computation spilling to CPU. Its higher-bit files leave much less room: Q5_K_M is 6.58 GB and Q6_K is 7.46 GB.

3. Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, Q6_K or Q8_0 GGUF
Official model: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507
Quantization files: https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Qwen_Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF

This is a useful compact, direct-response baseline. The official model is explicitly non-thinking, and the quantization table lists Q6_K at 3.31 GB and Q8_0 at 4.28 GB. It could give you more freedom to preserve weight precision while keeping a practical context budget. Its published instruction-following and tool-use results justify testing, but I found no direct retain comparison with gpt-oss-20b.

4. Ministral 3 8B Instruct 2512, Q4_K_M GGUF
Official model: https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512
Quantization files: https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512-GGUF/tree/main
Dated release: https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-3/

This offers a different dense-model family with native JSON output and function calling. The listed Q4_K_M language-model file is 5.2 GB. Use the text-only path for retain; the repository distributes vision projection files separately. The official FP8 configuration targets 12 GB VRAM, so the 8 GB proposal depends on further quantization and limited context. The family launch is dated December 2, 2025, before the question cutoff, although the exact currently listed quantization artifact was not independently dated.

5. llama.cpp schema-constrained output and explicit placement
Documentation: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md
Public source: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/include/llama.h
Windows/CUDA build guidance: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/build.md

This supporting mechanism may matter as much as the model choice: use the local chat endpoint with the required JSON schema, explicitly request all model layers on the GPU, and set a bounded context rather than inheriting a huge advertised maximum. The current server exposes GPU placement, automatic-fit, context and cache-type controls. Schema constraints can reduce format failures; they cannot ensure that the extracted entities, relationships or facts are correct.

How I would select among them

Start with one concurrent retain job and a modest context such as 4K, increasing it only to the size your actual prompts require. Include the output budget when choosing that limit. Inspect startup placement and memory reporting, then run a worst-case sample while observing dedicated GPU memory. A successful model load alone is insufficient. If memory is tight, reduce context or batch pressure, or move to the smaller model; investigate supported cache quantization as a separately measured tradeoff.

Compare a representative set of your own retain inputs against the existing gpt-oss-20b setup. Score valid schema output, missed facts, invented facts, entity/relationship consistency, latency and peak dedicated VRAM. Keep prompts and evaluation criteria fixed. The preferred choice is the smallest configuration that meets your extraction-quality threshold on those inputs. Ordinary CPU tokenization and request handling do not themselves imply model spill, so define the acceptance check around model weights and inference placement.

Evidence limits

All file sizes above are decimal GB as displayed by the publishers and exclude runtime allocations. Windows display use, context, buffers and concurrency can change fit. No model was downloaded or executed. Most evidence is from live pages whose full publication date was not established; I have not treated those pages as proven available by July 2, 2026. Native unauthenticated grep.app code search was attempted but inaccessible; public code was instead found through web indexing and the actual llama.cpp header was opened.
